data.narrative:
ClearSpace, a Series A+ space technology company founded by Luc Piguet and Muriel Richard, operates within the Space & Aerospace sector alongside a comparable universe of 5 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 identifiable private competitors including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Standard triangulation methods prove limited here. Peer-median valuation cannot be applied: while 14 same-sector peers exist, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier companies yields fewer than the 3 minimum datapoints required for statistical reliability. Public-comp anchoring is similarly inapplicable because ClearSpace's revenue is not disclosed—a typical constraint for private companies—and applying the sector's 27.4x median P/S multiple without this input would be speculative rather than grounded.

The absence of sufficient comparable private financings at the Series A+ stage in orbital/space infrastructure, combined with missing revenue data, prevents a defensible quantitative range. Any valuation of ClearSpace would require either: (1) revenue disclosure and application of public sector multiples with stage-appropriate discounting, or (2) access to recent Series A+ or Series B private rounds within debris remediation or satellite operations to establish peer financing benchmarks. The $36M raised to date establishes a floor for capital deployed but does not directly imply post-money valuation. Further diligence on unit economics and comparable exit multiples in the sector is necessary before a range can be responsibly offered.
